subject.title: fix: gateway boots when a configured plugin payload is broken

question: Should gateway readiness remain successful when a configured enabled plugin has a known payload-verification failure, with the plugin quarantined and surfaced as configured-unavailable?
rationale: This is a deliberate availability-versus-completeness contract for readiness probes and operators, not a mechanical correctness question that source inspection can settle.

options.title: Approve isolated degraded readiness
options.body: Accept the PR’s contract that a known plugin-owned payload failure disables only that plugin while gateway readiness remains successful and diagnostics expose the unavailable owner.

options.title: Retain fail-closed readiness
options.body: Keep the existing contract that any configured enabled plugin payload failure blocks readiness, using the merged diagnostic improvements from https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/110200 for actionable recovery.

recommendation.title: Approve isolated degraded readiness
recommendation.body: Accept the PR’s contract that a known plugin-owned payload failure disables only that plugin while gateway readiness remains successful and diagnostics expose the unavailable owner.

likelyOwner.reason: The timeline assigns this PR to steipete after the proof and prior ClawSweeper review identified an owner-level readiness decision.
